item.title: India's investments in US treasuries up $38.4 billion in June-August
item.description: India's investment in US Treasury securities increased USD 38.4 billion, or 21 per cent, between June and August, coinciding with substantial inflows of Foreign Currency Non-Resident (FCNR) (B) deposits into the Indian banking system. According to data compiled by PTI from the US Department of the Treasury, India's investment in US Treasuries rose to USD 219.7 billion in August 2026 from USD 181.3 billion in May 2026, just before the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) introduced the concessional facility. Gaura Sengupta, economist at IDFC First Bank, said the RBI's foreign exchange reserves increased during the period of FCNR(B) inflows, with a portion of the accretion being invested in US Treasury securities. The RBI had introduced a special USD-INR swap facility on June 8, 2026, to encourage foreign currency inflows and strengthen the country's balance of payments position. item.title: India's edible oil import bill rises 24% to record ₹2 trillion in 2025-26
item.description: India's edible oil imports rose 6 per cent to 16.92 million tonnes in the oil year ended October 2026, and the import bill jumped 24 per cent to about Rs 200,000 crore, the Solvent Extractors' Association of India (SEA) said on Monday. Edible oil imports in the 2025-26 oil year (November-October) increased compared with 16.01 million tonnes a year earlier, when the bill was about Rs 161,126 crore, the trade body said in a statement. Total vegetable oil imports, including non-edible oils, rose 5 per cent to 17.24 million tonnes from 16.36 million tonnes. India imports edible oils to bridge the gap between domestic supply and demand, a practice that began in the 1990s. Over the past 20 years, import volumes have risen 2.8 times, while the cost has risen nearly 15 times, SEA said. Refined oil imports fell sharply to 0.82 million tonnes in 2025-26 from 1.74 million tonnes a year earlier, SEA said. item.title: India's unemployment rate eases to eight-month low of 4.9% in October
item.description: India's unemployment rate declined marginally to 4.9 per cent in October from 5 per cent in September, as female labour force participation and workforce participation improved, particularly in rural areas, according to government data released on Monday. The overall unemployment rate for people aged 15 years and above was also 0.3 percentage points lower than the 5.2 per cent recorded in October 2025, the latest Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) bulletin released by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation showed. Overall urban unemployment declined to 6.7 per cent from 6.9 per cent in September, while rural unemployment remained unchanged at 4.2 per cent. The improvement was accompanied by an increase in the female Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR), which rose to 35 per cent in October from 34.6 per cent in September and 34.2 per cent a year earlier, reaching its highest level since February 2026. India's goods exports increased 45 per cent to USD 49.47 billion in October, compared to USD 34.11 billion in the same month last year. Imports also rose 16 per cent to USD 89.35 billion from USD 76.69 billion. As a result, trade deficit widened to a year high of USD 39.88 billion. item.title: India imports over half its edible oil, faces food risks: NITI Aayog VC
item.description: India is perhaps still not secure regarding its food supply across the various products, as the country is the world's largest importer of edible oils, NITI Aayog vice-chairman Ashok Kumar Lahiri said on Friday. Addressing an event here, Lahiri said India meets more than half of its edible oil needs through imports, and imports are estimated at 17 million metric tonnes, valued at about USD 20 billion. Similarly, India is both the world's largest producer and consumer of pulses, and accounts for roughly a fourth of total global pulse consumption, approximately 25 to 27 million tonnes annually. "We are talking about Viksit Krishi in Viksit Bharat in 2047. As we move towards Viksit Bharat at 2047, are we secure regarding our food supply across the various products?
